items.title: Paul Barbarin Interview, 1960-01-28
items.q: That Chapper Willett was one of the main arrangers. At the time I was with the big band there, wasn't out of college then.

ctx.x: What about, uh... Louis Armstrong? Did he have any arrangers when you worked with him?

Well, yeah, he had, uh... Chapper Willett, and, well, a few others, I mean. Yeah. That Chapper Willett was one of the main arrangers. At the time I was with the big band there, wasn't out of college then.

items.title: Paul Barbarin Interview, 1957-03-27
items.q: Well I think Happy was older than Louie. Yeah, he's an older boy than Louie.

ctx.x: What about Red Happy? When did he come up with? Who was that? Red Happy. I heard once he was like a kid with Louie and the Reform school. Well yeah. Louie's age or older?
Well I think Happy was older than Louie. Yeah, he's an older boy than Louie. What was his real name?

items.title: Paul Barbarin Interview, 1959-12-23
items.q: But when you came back here from leaving Louis?

ctx.x: He passed in Kentucky, didn't he? At his hometown. I don't know. Well, Lee Blatt, he played the guitar, but he didn't have no amplifier, I'm sure that.
But when you came back here from leaving Louis?
Well, then I found that amplifier, yeah.
